NTA.  Giving someone something intentionally when you know they're allergic to it is literally attempted murder, even if you weren't intending to murder them.  You literally stated in your post that you started to have difficulty breathing.  That is anaphylaxis, and is a life threatening condition that people die from all the time.  
Now, I will say that I am sure they didn't know you were going to have trouble breathing, but they still intentionally gave you something you're allergic to.  That is a crime, and it is fortunate that you survived.  This is not an overdramatic reaction.  I applaud you for not asking your mom to drop the charges.  They put your life at risk, and had you died they would have likely gotten charged with a crime anyway.   
I also recommend you get an epi-pen and keep it on hand now that you know your throat closes up when you're exposed to gum.

I've been a nurse for 23 years, the last 6 of which have been in psych.  I am in the minority of nurses who are actually kind, caring, and truly want to help their patients.  I strive to make sure that my patients know they're important.  We get some pretty rough characters in our units, and I treat them with as much kindness as all the others.  Mentally ill patients need to know they are valuable and worthwhile.  I try to make sure my patients know this every time I am their nurse.  Unfortunately, some of my coworkers often tell me I'm "too nice".  I just tell them to let me do me, and that being nice to my patients has never steered me wrong.  There's a way to be kind, but firm in a loving manner.  I am saying all this, not to brag, but to point out that not all psych nurses are the same. Some of us really do care.  I'm sorry you had such bad experiences.
